lines.content: - Use imperative mood in the subject line (e.g., "Add feature" not "Added feature").
- Separate subject from body with a blank line.
- Limit the subject line to 50 characters.
- Explain "what" and "why" in the body, not "how" (the code shows how).
- Use meaningful variable and method names.
- Keep methods short and focused on a single responsibility.
- Use Javadoc for all public classes and methods.
- Avoid overly complex logic within methods.
- Order class members logically (fields, constructor, methods).
This is a project template for a greenfield Java project. It's named after the Java mascot _Duke_. Given below are instructions on how to use it.
Prerequisites: JDK 25, update Intellij to the most recent version.
1. Open Intellij (if you are not in the welcome screen, click `File` > `Close Project` to close the existing project first)
1. Open the project into Intellij as follows:
1. Select the project directory, and click `OK`.
1. If there are any further prompts, accept the defaults.
1. Configure the project to use **JDK 25** (not other versions) as explained in [here](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/idea/sdk.html#set-up-jdk).
In the same dialog, set the **Project language level** field to the `SDK default` option.

1. After that, locate the `src/main/java/Wiz.java` file, right-click it, and choose `Run Duke.main()` (if the code editor is showing compile errors, try restarting the IDE). If the setup is correct, you should see something like the below as the output:

This project follows a test coverage target of 50%. JUnit tests are required to verify the behavior of the code.
